# Red Whistle

A small red emergency whistle carried by Chen from the old neighborhood. It
is an ordinary object; its connection to the 2013 storm is part of Chen's
fragmentary memory, not an objective conclusion supplied by the engine.

My unresolved obligations were to learn exactly what the permit said, determine whether it truly connected to the storm, and follow up with Gao Rui, Lin Yao, and Qiao Shun.

I went to the student union office to resolve the missing audit-packet labels because a small accounting mistake could cost people their stipends. I had wanted Qiao to review the numbers with me, but I was afraid of a spoken refusal and had kept that request unsent. I inspected and read the packet: it contained reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction. I initially tried to message Qiao, but the attempt failed because I used an invalid recipient form; nothing changed. Qiao then asked me to walk through the figures and the basis for the correction, saying he had fifteen minutes before leaving to care for his sibling. I asked which rows fed each total and what supported the correction. I searched the office and found only brass-key and union-audit, with no receipts or additional financial records. I told Qiao that I could not identify the figures, source rows, or supporting basis from the packet and would not invent labels or approve it. He said he could not identify them either, asked that the packet be marked pending, and left for his sibling’s care schedule. I labeled the packet: “PENDING — missing source rows, figures, receipts, and basis for handwritten correction; do not approve.” The packet is now pending, and I still owe myself and the union the missing documentation and a proper verification. I tried to contact Chen Mo for that documentation, but that attempt also failed because I used an invalid recipient form; nothing changed. I am waiting until 2026-03-16T07:31:35+08:00.

I must obtain documentary support rather than approve the packet.

I remember examining the 2013 storm ledger and reading it alongside the machine-generated original export. The ledger records storm calls, equipment checkout, and an incomplete witness line. The export’s timestamps disagree with the summary sheet; comparing them confirmed that the two records contain different information. Searching the campus archive found only the original export and storm ledger, with no supporting provenance material. I tried to go to the harbor archive, but it was closed, so I waited instead. Chen later messaged that he had found an old neighborhood permit marked with a narrow flood-route annotation and still had a red whistle from that time. I remember being nine when Chen promised to stay, then left and did not return for what felt like an hour; I do not remember the adult he brought back. I am uncertain whether the permit or whistle connects to that day or to the ledger’s incomplete witness line. I must verify the records’ provenance before sharing or publishing anything.

My private copy of the permit is still overdue and unresolved. I intend to verify the ledger’s provenance and discrepancies and locate and file the permit before discussing anything publicly.
